# Establishment log — popol-vuh-019 (image 0059 last line, 0060, 0061, 0062 to about line 20)

Read 2026-11-27 by the routine's own model from source/pages/i0059 (its last line, `are ta cu xahauax chique`),
all of i0060 and i0061, and i0062 to `… ta xqueleh.` (about its twentieth line), in strips of about seven lines at
~1×, with 1.6–3× crops of doubtful words, checked word by word against Brasseur 1861 (OCR lines c. 25590–25960: his
chapter 9 from `Are ta cu x-ahauax chique qaholab` to `ta x-qu'eleh`, just before `LAHPAH CHI TZIH`). Pillow in a
scratch venv. Note: on 0061 and 0062 the K'iche' column runs further right than on 0060; crops must be taken to
about x=1600 or line ends are lost (caught and re-read this run).

Start: `Are ta cu xahauax chique ꜭaholab` (0059, last line). End: `“Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha ꜭaholab, ta xqueleh.` on 0062,
followed by an indented paragraph `Xe oc chi cut pa Teuh Ha …` (the Cold House; Brasseur's chapter 10), which begins
popol-vuh-020. parts.json: 020 set to images 0062–0065 (was 0066–0068, which would have left 0062–0065 unread);
plan.md row updated. Image 0063 not needed.

Content: the lords want the boys killed at the ball game but are beaten again; they play with the boys' ball; the lords
count their losses and demand four bowls of flowers (cacamuchih, zaqui muchit, cana muchit, carinimac) by dawn; the
boys are sent into Chaim Ha, the House of Blades, the second trial; they promise the blades the flesh of all animals
and the blades stop; at night they call the ants (Chai zanic, Chequen zanic) to fetch the flowers from the garden of
Huncame and Vvcub Came; the guardians (Puhuyu birds) sing `Xpurpuvec`, `Puhuyu` and do not notice the ants cutting
their tails and wings; the four bowls are full at dawn; the boys bring them to the lords, who pale; the guardians'
lips are split for it — the Purpuec's split beak to this day; the ball game again, ending level, adjourned to the next
morning.

Paragraphs: ours, at the sense joints (as 015–018). No heading in this stretch.

## Folios
0060 carries `25` at the top left (= 25v), 0062 `26` at the top left (= 26v); so 0059 = 25r, 0061 = 26r →
`fols. 25r–26v`. 0061 also carries `31` at the top right in a different hand — a later foliation; not used.

## Supralinear / corrections
- 0060 l.1–2: Ximénez wrote `ri hun chi` and struck it; then `ri` + caret + `chiri` at the start of the next line
  (the caret and a mark above `chiri` suggest it was added). Printed `ri chiri chi cha`; B. `ri chiri chi chaa`.
- 0061 margin, beside `re ca zicouic` (l.~32): a large X in dark ink — later hand; ignored.
- 0062 l.6: a heavy blot after `chahal`; nothing under it seems lost (B. `x-e uchax chahal?`).
- 0060 l.20: a small blot after `qui cha`; printed `qui cha` (B. `qui cha`).

## Plain c kept where Brasseur has g/q (unmarked ejectives stay unmarked; the letter is a clear plain c at 2–3×)
`acab` ×2 and `chacab` (B. agab, ch'agab; as 015's `xa hun acab`; 018 had printed `aꜫab`), `acaba` (B. Agaba),
`acabil` (B. agabil), `cana muchit` (B. gana), `catacox` (B. gatacox), `elecaxic` ×3, `elecai` (B. elegaxic, elegai),
`xaloc` (B. xalog; as 015), `chu cab tac che` (B. chu gab tak), `zicou`, `zicouic` (B. ziqou), `ca tucuvic`
(B. tuguvic; letters doubtful), `choquic` ×2 (B. ch'ogic; as 017), `camol` (B. qamol; as 018), `cama`, `cam vla`
(B. qama, qam).
Cuatrillo/tresillo where the hand shows the g/q shape: `ꜭha ri hun`, `ca ꜭha ahau`, `qui ꜭhabeh` (B. chabeh),
`e ꜭo`, `cuꜭ`, `ca ꜭux qui he`, `ꜫuz v vach` (q-shaped; B. guz; as 015/018's ꜫuz).

## Letters decided by Brasseur (hand ambiguous)
- `huticab` ×4 (MS looks `huhcab` with an i-dot over the second h: t written like h, as 017's petic/tic; B. huticab).
- `v tiohil` (MS `vhohil`, t like h; B. u tiohil), `ticon` ×4 (MS `hcon`), `tiquitoh` (MS `hquitoh`), `Qui tique laon`
  (MS `quihque laon`).
- `Ma ba quix bec` (MS looks `mabu`; a/u ambiguous; B. Ma-ba). `cu ri coꜩih` (MS looks `cari`; B. curi).
- `Vvcub Came` ×3 as in 018 (v/u indistinguishable in this hand).

## Readings against Brasseur (image followed)
- `chi cha` (B. chi chaa — MS has one a; could be cha 'blade' or chaa 'ball court'; the drafter should weigh both).
- `ca ca coho` (B. ka coho: one ca fewer).
- `Xa ca cha ca cah cah ꜩel coꜩih` (MS `xacachara cah / cah ꜩel`; the fourth letter of `chaca` could be r; B. `xa-cucha
  ca kah cah tzel cotzih`). Doubtful word division; `cah ꜩel coꜩih` = 'four bowls of flowers' is clear.
- `zaqui muchit` (B. zaki-muchih) — the MS has `muchit` for the second and third flowers, `muchih` for the first.
- `chi ia` and `mix ia` (MS `chiia`, `mi / xia`; B. ch'y ya, m'yx ya): printed with Ximénez's i.
- `quix petoc` (B. qu'yx pe-ne): the MS clearly has `petoc`.
- `oh i cama` (MS `ohicama`; B. oh y qama).
- `ca ca cah vloc` (MS `cacacah`; B. ca cu kah uloc).
- `Xpurpuvec, Xpurpuvec` (MS second time `xpurpu-/uec`; u/v); `Purpuec` (0062).
- `xe zaccah e` (MS `xezaccahe`; B. x-e zakcah e).
- `zamahel taconel` (MS `zamahel ta-/conel`; B. reads `(akone!` — OCR damage).

## Speaker tags
- `“He na qui cut,” xa xeꜭha ꜭaholab.` — punctuated by the house reading (a xꜭha tag closes the speech before it), which
  gives the line to the boys; Brasseur makes `He na qui cut … cotzih` one speech of Xibalba ('let them go then … four
  bowls of flowers'). Open for the drafter; logged in QUESTIONS.md.
- `zacaric chic, xeꜭha Xibalba` (end): left as narrative + tag ('for the morning, said Xibalba'), as Brasseur.

## Doubtful
chiri (caret), chi cha, xa ca cha ca cah, huticab, cana muchit, chi ia, acaba, chacab, ca tucuvic, elecai, ca ca cah,
Libah chi (B. Libahchi), taconel. No gaps.
